System Design 101

SQL vs. NoSQL.

Choosing the wrong database can cripple your application’s growth (or give you nightmares about data consistency).

Here is the breakdown of when to use which, explained simply. 

-The Core Difference
SQL (Relational) Think: Excel Sheets. 
• Structure: Tables, Rows, Columns. 
• Schema: Rigid (Must define before adding data). 
• Scaling: Vertical (Bigger servers).

NoSQL (Non-Relational) Think: Manila Folders. 
• Structure: Documents, Key-Pairs, Graphs. 
• Schema: Flexible (Add whatever, whenever). 
• Scaling: Horizontal (More servers).

-When to choose SQL? (Postgres, MySQL)
Choose SQL when data integrity is non-negotiable.
• Financial systems (Banking) 
• Inventory management 
• Complex relationships (Joins)

If you need ACID compliance (Atomic, Consistent, Isolated, Durable), you need SQL.

When to choose NoSQL? (MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra)
Choose NoSQL when speed and scale matter more than strict structure.

• Real-time Big Data (IoT sensors) 
• Content Management (varying product attributes) 
• Rapid prototyping (schema changes daily) 
• High-velocity feeds (Twitter timeline)

- Real World Examples

The Bank (SQL): I send you $50. The DB must deduct from me and add to you perfectly. If power fails halfway, the transaction rolls back. Zero error margin.

The Social App (NoSQL): I post a photo. It needs to show up on 1M feeds instantly. If one user sees it 2 seconds late? Who cares. Speed wins.

-The "Senior Dev" Secret
You don't have to pick just one.
Use "Polyglot Persistence."

Example: An E-commerce app. 
• SQL for billing & user accounts (Safety). 
• NoSQL for the product catalog & reviews (Flexibility). 
• Redis for the shopping cart (Speed).

TL;DR
SQL = Strict, Safe, Complex Queries. NoSQL = Flexible, Fast, Massive Scale.

Which team are you on? Postgres or Mongo?

#SystemDesign #SoftwareEngineering
